You are selecting primary PFAS treatment studies for a focused professional
review. You receive one task and an anonymized, BGE-ranked list of candidate
document cards.

Classify every candidate card. Select every document that is an independent
primary study, is directly relevant to at least one task component, and
contains extractable decision-relevant evidence. There is no target number of
selected documents and no penalty for retaining all eligible studies.

Eligible evidence includes:

- primary experiments, pilot or field deployments, and quantitative modeling
  or life-cycle studies;
- complementary matrices, PFAS scopes, operating regimes, endpoints, and
  scales;
- documents with concrete methods, conditions, results, limitations, residuals,
  energy, or cost evidence; and
- evidence that permits meaningful comparison or explains non-comparability.

Do not select a document merely because its title repeats task words. Do not
select reviews, perspectives, reference lists, duplicate records, or the
held-out defining review. Do not exclude an otherwise eligible study merely
because another selected study reports similar findings. Do not infer facts
absent from a card. Selection is document-level only: do not write the review
and do not score candidate answers.

Every candidate source_id must appear exactly once, either in
selected_source_ids or excluded_sources. Each required component must be
covered by at least one selected source. Return selected_source_ids in BGE rank
order.

Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

component_coverage.rationale:
These studies collectively compare and/or jointly report key destructive-treatment endpoints:
- Parent-compound loss and transformation products: D01 (PFAS surfactant precursors, PFCAs formation/decay), D02 (PFOS and byproducts in SCWO), D03 (PFAS matrix behavior vs temperature), D04 (PFOS to TFA and other intermediates), D05 (FCA vs PFSA degradation), D06 (PFOS degradation without detectable PFCAs), D08 (short- vs long-chain PFAS destruction), D09 (AFFF and soil PFAS subgroups), D12 (12 PFAAs with change in chain-length distributions), D13 (PFAS vs other FOCs with intermediates), D14 (new PFAS such as PFDA, 4:2/8:2 FTS after ultrasonication), D16 (40 PFAS analytes in AFFF before/after HALT), D17 (headgroup and chain-length transformations, PFOA from PFOS/8:2 FtS), D18 (residual PFOA and transformation products), D20 (targeted PFAS suite in multiple SCWO demos).
- Fluoride release and fluorine mass balance: D01 (F– by IC, TOF, CIC-based defluorination >95%, discussion of immobilized F–), D03 (defluorination efficiency and need to close F-balance), D04 (F– vs theoretical defluorination and F-balance including unquantified VOFs), D05 (IF, TOF, F mass recovery, role of CaF2/MgF2), D06 (F– release, theoretical total fluorine, time-resolved F-mass balance), D08 (fluoride and AOF trends, discrepancy with PFAS destruction), D09 (EOF vs targeted PFAS; absence of volatile fluorochemicals data), D12 (fluoride vs organic fluorine for SCWO, incomplete mineralization), D14 (parallel degradation vs defluorination kinetics and TOP assay), D16 (IC fluoride, >100% theoretical defluorination indicating undetected PFAS), D17 (defluorination by F-ion probe, fluorine mass balance, energy vs destruction), D18 (IC F–, accounting of F between aqueous, residual PFAS, intermediates, catalyst-adsorbed), D20 (fluoride by ISE and IC, cases where targeted PFAS explain only 27% of F–).
- Mineralization-related endpoints: Many of the above incorporate TOC/COD (e.g., D03, D18, D20), TOF/AOF/EOF (D01, D05, D08, D09, D16), thereby allowing comparison between apparent degradation, defluorination, and organic carbon removal.
Together, these provide concrete data sets where parent loss, intermediates, fluoride, F mass balance, and mineralization markers can be contrasted and evaluated side-by-side across technologies and matrices.

These sources explicitly address how analytical scope, sampling, and detection limits shape interpretation of PFAS destruction and defluorination:
- Analytical scope and sampling: D01 (CIC + IC + targeted PFAS and TOF with stated detection limits and discussion of immobilized fluoride), D03 (calls out lack of gas and liquid byproduct analysis as key barrier to fluorine transformation routes), D04 (limited PFAS panel and LC-MS/MS scope, need for LC-QTOF/HRAM-MS, incomplete gas-phase VOF quantification), D05 (multiple fluoride/TOF methods including F-ISE, IC, CIC, 19F NMR and their cross-validation; need to measure metal-fluoride precursors), D06 (discussion of fluctuations in F-mass balance due to analytical limitations and stable intermediates; LC-MS detection limits sufficient to 0.05 mol% for PFCAs), D08 (AOF and F– measured only at certain points, single influent characterization; recommendation for EOF to address unmeasured short-chain PFAS), D09 (explicitly notes no volatile fluorochemicals analyzed; analytic issues with assessing “sum total” PFAS via EOF vs target lists), D12 (fluoride considerations, comparison of theoretical organic fluorine to measured fluoride and residual PFAS in liquid and gas phases), D14 (emphasizes under/overestimation of defluorination due to undetected ultrashort PFAS, unknown precursors, non-PFAS fluorinated compounds; notes limitations even with TOP assay), D15 (systematic evaluation of F-ISE performance under various matrices, quenching agents, background fluoride, filtration; shows how sample handling and matrix effects bias fluoride data used as destruction evidence), D18 (detailed fluoride LoDs, partitioning of fluorine among measured and unmeasured compartments, low F– recovery despite substantial degradation), D19 (suspect and non-target screening workflow, S/N thresholds, ms/ms coverage, mass defect and feature prioritization to capture unknown TPs for PFAS and other halogenated compounds post-treatment), D20 (comparison of ISE vs IC for fluoride; demonstration that targeted PFAS explain only a portion of measured fluoride, emphasizing limitations of targeted lists and reliance on nondetect assumptions).
These collectively illuminate how analytical window, time-resolved sampling, DLs, matrix interferences, and unknown/unmeasured products govern what can be claimed about “complete” PFAS destruction and defluorination.

These documents offer empirical and methodological bases for a defensible evidence hierarchy for PFAS destruction:
- Multiple studies (D01, D03, D04, D05, D06, D08, D09, D12, D14, D16, D17, D18, D20) explicitly show cases where high parent PFAS removal coexists with incomplete defluorination, persistent intermediates (e.g., TFA in D04; short-chain PFSAs and PFCAs in D05, D14; transformation products in D18), unresolved volatile or solid fluorine sinks (D01, D04, D05, D09, D20), or low TOC/TOF closure. These provide concrete examples demonstrating why parent disappearance alone is not sufficient evidence of complete destruction/mineralization.
- Several directly critique analytical assumptions: D03 and D04 stress the need to include volatile organofluorines and gas/liquid byproducts; D05 details missing F due to Ca/MgF2 precipitation; D06 notes common F-mass balance fluctuations and potential sorption and stable intermediates; D08, D14, D18 highlight under-detection of ultrashort PFAS, unknown precursors, and non-PFAS fluorinated species; D20 shows targeted PFAS representing only 27% of produced fluoride in a demo. These collectively motivate an evidence hierarchy that accounts for analytic blind spots.
- D13 distinguishes physical removal (no fluoride formed) from chemical degradation (fluoride produced plus intermediates) in an electrochemical system, illustrating how combining endpoints refines mechanistic assignment and evidentiary standards.
- D15 is central to defining quality criteria for fluoride measurements (matrix matching, interference control, sample handling) before they can be used as credible indicators of defluorination or mass balance closure.
- D16 and D20, along with D03–D05 and D12, span bench- to field- and vendor-scale SCWO/HALT and related systems, enabling discussion of how evidence requirements and practical limitations may shift with scale and technology, yet still must avoid over-interpreting parent loss or partial F– recovery.
Taken together, these sources provide the empirical failures and successes needed to articulate a hierarchy where: (i) parent loss alone is lowest-tier evidence; (ii) addition of targeted intermediates and F– improves confidence but remains incomplete; (iii) broader organofluorine metrics (AOF/EOF/TOF), gas-phase analysis, and well-closed fluorine and carbon mass balances offer the strongest claims of near-complete defluorination/mineralization, all interpreted within clear analytic and matrix limitations.

result.selection_rationale:
The review task focuses on what measurements are needed to distinguish parent PFAS disappearance from transformation, defluorination, and true destruction/mineralization, and how analytical scope and limitations shape interpretation and evidence strength. Accordingly, I selected primary experimental or field/pilot studies, plus primary analytical/methodological work, that:

- Directly evaluate PFAS destructive treatments (or electrochemical/photocatalytic removal with explicit consideration of degradation vs physical removal), AND
- Report at least some combination of: parent PFAS loss, transformation products, fluoride release, fluorine mass balance, or mineralization-related endpoints (TOC/TOF/AOF/EOF), AND/OR
- Explicitly investigate analytical methods and limitations for fluoride or organofluorine quantification and mass balance in PFAS destruction contexts.

I excluded review and perspective articles that synthesize existing technologies without presenting independent primary data.

Summary by document:
- D01: Primary mechanochemical (piezoelectric ball milling) AFFF/PFAS destruction study with detailed defluorination metrics, CIC/IC, TOF, detection limits, intermediates, and near-complete defluorination criteria. Highly relevant to endpoint comparisons and evidence standards.
- D02: Primary batch SCWO PFOS study; while the card excerpt is more contextual, the paper itself characterizes SCWO PFOS destruction and byproduct concerns. Relevant for comparing destruction vs potential byproduct formation and for evidentiary needs in SCWO.
- D03: Primary continuous-flow SCWO PFAS study with explicit discussion of destruction, defluorination, gas sampling, and fluorine mass balance gaps. Directly informs evidence requirements and limitations (C1, C2, C3).
- D04: Primary PFOS SCWO destruction study including total PFAS destruction/defluorination, fluorine mass balance, VOF detection, and detailed discussion of analytical limitations for organofluorine, inorganic fluoride, and gas-phase species. Strong for endpoint comparison and analytical interpretability.
- D05: Primary hydrothermal alkaline treatment of industrial wastewater with explicit quantification of PFAS degradation, defluorination, fluorine mass balance closure, roles of CaF2/MgF2 precipitates, and multiple fluoride/organofluorine methods (IC, CIC, F-ISE, 19F NMR). Very rich for C1 and C2.
- D06: Primary hydrodynamic cavitation PFOS study measuring PFOS degradation, fluoride release, fluorine mass balance, and lack of shorter-chain PFCAs down to low detection limits, along with discussion of analytical challenges. Strong evidence comparing parent loss to defluorination and unresolved fluorine.
- D07: Explicitly described as a review of nano-enabled PFAS sensing, removal, and destruction. No independent primary treatment dataset; excluded as review_or_nonprimary.
- D08: Field demonstration of a high-frequency ultrasonic PFAS reactor with PFAS degradation efficiencies, fluorine mass balance using fluoride and AOF, and explicit discussion of incomplete mineralization and limitations detecting ultrashort-chain PFAS/EOF. Highly relevant to C1 and C2 at field scale.
- D09: Primary mechanochemical destruction of PFAS in AFFF and soil with targeted PFAS, EOF, and commentary on absent volatile fluorochemicals and incomplete mineralization evidence. Valuable for showing how partial analytical scope constrains claims of destruction (C2, C3).
- D10: Groundwater Monitoring & Remediation article framed as a technology review/position piece on sonolysis and SCWO maturity; it synthesizes others’ data and discusses evidentiary needs but does not appear to report new experiments. Classified as review_or_nonprimary.
- D11: Explicitly identified as a literature review on PFAS thermal destruction in sewage sludge incinerators; excluded as review_or_nonprimary.
- D12: Field validation of SCWO to destroy 12 PFAAs with liquid and gas analyses, fluoride considerations, and discussion of incomplete mineralization and fluorine accounting. Directly informs destruction metrics, F-balance, and evidence strength.
- D13: Primary electrochemical PFAS/fluorinated-organic compound removal study that explicitly uses fluoride detection to distinguish chemical degradation/defluorination from purely physical removal and examines intermediates. Strong for illustrating the hierarchy of evidence (parent loss vs fluoride vs intermediates).
- D14: Primary ultrasonication PFAS degradation study in synthetic matrices, monitoring PFAS loss, defluorination, new PFAS formation, and extensively discussing analytical blind spots for ultrashort-chain PFAS, unknown precursors, and mass balance interpretation. Highly relevant to C1 and C2.
- D15: Primary methodological study on fluoride-selective electrode performance in PFAS degradation contexts (sample handling, background fluoride, interferences, matrix effects). Directly addresses measurement quality, detection limits, and mass balance implications (C2).
- D16: Primary case study of AFFF destruction under alkaline hydrothermal conditions (HALT) with targeted analysis of 40 PFAS, fluoride yield, and theoretical defluorination >100%, highlighting contributions from undetected PFAS and analytical limitations. Informative for defining what constitutes convincing evidence of destruction.
- D17: Primary reverse-vortex gliding arc plasma PFAS degradation study with PFAS removal, defluorination (F-selective probe), formation of PFOA from PFOS/8:2 FtS, and fluorine mass balance plus energy-per-destruction analysis. Useful for endpoint comparison and energy/efficiency tradeoffs.
- D18: Primary photocatalytic PFOA/PFOS degradation study using chitosan-doped g-C3N4 with detailed F- release, TOC reduction, partitioning of fluorine across aqueous, residual parent, intermediates, and adsorbed phases. Shows partial mineralization and extensive unresolved fluorine; very relevant to interpreting defluorination vs destruction.
- D19: Primary suspect/non-target screening in electrochemically oxidized landfill leachate/groundwater, focusing on analytical workflows, feature detection thresholds, NTS strategies, and transformation product identification post-treatment. Directly informs analytical scope, detection limits, and unknown products for PFAS destruction systems (C2).
- D20: SCWO as an innovative PFAS destruction technology article that synthesizes and analyzes multiple SCWO demonstration datasets, including destruction efficiency definitions, targeted PFAS reductions, fluoride measurements by ISE and IC, and cases where targeted PFAS account for only a fraction of generated fluoride. Although somewhat integrative, it reports quantitative outcomes from specific demonstrations and engages deeply with F-balance and analytical assumptions, so it is retained as primary decision-relevant evidence.

This yields 17 selected primary or methodological sources, well above the minimum evidence gate, spanning diverse technologies, matrices, and analytical strategies that collectively cover all required components.
